summary.text: A Gu set is a group of Gu worms built around one core, with other Gu chosen to support that core and chain into one system.

claims.text: The Gu on Fang Yuan were all gathered individually, so they could not form into a set. That collection did not cover all grounds, which severely affected his battle strength. He treats Shang clan city as the time to get a Gu worm set and to create a battle style with it.
He tells Bai Ning Bing that a set of complementary Gu worms is what lets them display their true power.

By rank three a Gu Master has to determine a direction and create a set of Gu worms along that line. Wei Yang names six aspects for that choice: attack, defense, healing, storage, movement, and investigative.

Forming the set has feeding, use, and refinement gains. Similar Gu share similar food, so that food is easier to collect, store, and trade. In use, the worms can be paired to raise ability or cover a weakness; rainbow light Gu has heavy expenditure, and light source Gu reduces that weakness. In refinement, placing similar Gu together saves money and has a higher chance of success than refining an array of mixed Gu.

For an attack direction, an attack type Gu has to be the core. Wei Yang’s example is Xiao Yan’s red fire Gu, then duplicate Gu, enlarge Gu, fire source Gu, and fire discharge Gu around it. Wei Yang himself is a movement type Gu Master whose core Gu worm is rainbow light Gu.
The creatures in the set are covered on Gu worms.

If the core is destroyed in refinement, the entire set collapses, so Wei Yang’s first advice is to convert that core into a vital Gu. One core is not enough: several important support Gu are needed, and a wrong choice will not let the core display its full value. When strength path flourished in ancient times, many more Gu complemented all-out effort Gu; most of those are extinct, so that set cannot be assembled by ancient methods and has to be explored.

Fang Yuan’s strength path plan uses all-out effort Gu as the core, with self-reliance Gu and bitter strength Gu as the support. With a few other Gu accompanying those three, he treats the set as initial success. Greater success, in that plan, waits on useful Gu from the three kings inheritance.

Using a support Gu as the core is quite rare. Most Gu Masters use support Gu in the set as assistance to the core Gu. Wei Yang’s own pattern is the ordinary one: rainbow light Gu, a movement Gu, as the core, with offensive broadsword light Gu as a main support and light source Gu as another support. All-out effort Gu is a support Gu that can still fill the core position.
Bai Ning Bing’s killer move ice blade storm uses revolving Gu paired with whirlwind Gu and ice blade Gu, forming an icy tornado. Using several Gu together as one technique is covered on killer moves.
Once all-out effort Gu, bitter strength Gu, and self-reliance Gu are together, the Gu set that Fang Yuan planned earlier has already reached initial success, forming the skeleton.

At Ku Mo’s level, the Gu set he created was completely customised for himself, using his battle style, his understanding of the bone path, and his understanding of battles and Gu Masters. Fang Yuan judges that if he inherited that set, the battle strength he could display would not be half of Ku Mo’s. Wu Gui’s other Gu were mixed among different paths and were a mess, unlike Ku Mo and Tie Mu Bai’s complete Gu set.

At a shop Fang Yuan finds strength path Gu in only three kinds, jin strength Gu, jun strength Gu, and beast strength Gu, and most are for attacking. Defense, investigation, and assistance are scarce there, so he judges it hard to create a Gu set from just strength path Gu. That shop’s soul path stock has Gu across those aspects, and he reads forming them into a set as letting the worms help each other and obtain greater effects. He takes Chu Du, a strength path Gu Immortal who still used other Gu for defense, investigation, and storage, as an example.
